cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: Allocate approximately 1 minute per mark: a 3-mark question gets about 3 minutes; leave 5–10 minutes at the end for checking

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: Attempt every question — there are no negative marks; even an educated guess on a multiple-choice question is worthwhile

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: Check answers systematically: re-read the question, verify units, confirm calculations, and apply reasonableness checks

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: When checking, work backwards from your answer or use an alternative method to verify; if both methods agree, the answer is likely correct

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: Know your calculator: enter data lists for mean and SD, use the nCr button for binomial coefficients, and use the fraction button for exact values

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: The formula sheet provides key formulas but not explanations; know when and how to apply each formula before the exam

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: For the statistics calculator paper: enter raw data into lists to find mean, SD, median, Q1, Q3 directly; this saves time and reduces arithmetic errors

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: Active revision strategies outperform passive reading: use past papers, flashcards, self-testing, and teaching others (retrieval practice)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: Spaced practice: revise a topic, revisit it after 1 day, then 3 days, then 1 week; this strengthens long-term memory more than cramming

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: Create a glossary of key terms with definitions; many marks are lost through imprecise use of statistical vocabulary

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: Practise full papers under timed conditions to build stamina and identify which topics take longest

cards.front: Recall a key point about Paper Technique Revision
cards.back: Keep a ‘mistakes log’: record every error from practice papers with the correct method — this targets revision to weak areas

cards.front: What should you know about gcse statistics exam tips — paper technique & revision?
cards.back: 1. For Paper Technique & Revision questions, show every step of your working clearly — method marks count even if the final answer is wrong 2. Check your answer makes sense in context (estimation, units, reasonableness) 3. Use correct mathematical notation and state formulae before substituting values 4. If a Paper Technique & Revision question asks you to 'prove' or 'show', write a logical chain of reasoning with a conclusion line 5. For problem-solving, identify the topic first, then recall the relevant method
Describe a complete revision and exam strategy for GCSE Statistics that maximises your grade.
